body:
Prompt injection risk: Untrusted rendered workflow prompt (includes PR-controlled content) is written verbatim into the model-routing conversation JSON and used to route model/effort; an attacker can embed instructions in PR text to influence routing decisions (e.g., pick a more expensive model or different effort), undermining the intended cost objective. Cross-file: enabled by model-routing in .github/workflows/mattpocock-skills-reviewer.md and consumed here. --- The best fix is to enforce a **defensive normalization/filtering step** before writing the routing conversation: strip known high-risk instruction-shaping patterns and cap prompt size, while preserving enough task context for routing. This keeps existing functionality (building a routing conversation from rendered prompt files) but reduces attacker influence from PR text.

In .github/workflows/mattpocock-skills-reviewer.lock.yml, update the inline Node script in the **“Prepare model-routing conversation”** step (around line 1284). Add:

  • a small sanitizer function to remove obvious instruction-overrides and role-injection markers (e.g., “ignore previous instructions”, role tags like system:/assistant:),
  • length limiting to prevent oversized adversarial payloads,
  • fallback to a safe default if sanitization empties the prompt.

No imports are needed beyond existing fs and path requires already in that inline script.
